subject: High-availability annex and order form language for EdgeBank
messages:
From: Anna Gonzalez <anna.gonzalez@edgebank.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: EdgeBank Procurement <procurement@edgebank.com>
Date: Sun, 7 Sep 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: HA annex + order form language we need for procurement

Marcus —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement and our infra team asked me to follow up with a concrete ask: we need explicit order form language and an HA annex that maps uptime/latency commitments to the order form and the enterprise MSA. Key items they want addressed before routing to legal and vendor management: 

- Clear uptime SLO(s) per region and the service credit schedule if carved-out thresholds are missed
- Latency targets (p95) for short inference sequences (<512 tokens) and for long sequences (>=512 tokens)
- Regional failover behavior (how Redwood routes traffic if a region is degraded) and any multi-region warm standby guarantees
- Data residency affirmation for us-east-1 and audit log retention for 1 year
- A one-time evidence packet to validate baseline telemetry during the pilot

We can attach the EdgeBank order form template once we have Redwood’s suggested language. Can you share a proposal or draft annex by Wed 9/10? Procurement wants to get this into the loop for a Sep signature window.

Anna Gonzalez
Director, Cloud Procurement | EdgeBank
anna.gonzalez@edgebank.com
[Attachment: EdgeBank_OrderForm_Template.pdf (pdf)]

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Gonzalez <anna.gonzalez@edgebank.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 8 Sep 2025 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: HA annex + order form language we need for procurement

Anna —

Thanks — appreciate the clear list. I’m looping in Kimberly (legal) and Aditya (sales) to draft language that can live in the order form + an HA annex attached to the MSA. Preliminary plan: I’ll propose explicit order-form snippets for the SLO and credits table, and Kimberly will review annex wording around exceptions and measurement. Aditya, can you confirm whether we can support a 1-year telemetry evidence packet as part of the onboarding pilot?

I’ll aim to send a first-pass draft by EOD Tue 9/9 so you can circulate to procurement on Wed. Expect the draft to include:

- SLO table: Regional availability measured monthly; uptime tiers (99.99 / 99.9 / 99.0) mapped to credits
- Latency commitments: p95 <= 250ms for <512-token inference in us-east-1 under baseline throughput; p95 <= 450ms for >=512 tokens (we’ll document measurement method)
- Regional failover: automatic routing to warm standby region; failover window and any additional RTO/RPO caveats
- Evidence: onboarding telemetry snapshot + playbook for audit logs and retention

Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai
[Attachment: HA_Annex_Draft_v1.docx (docx)]

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 9 Sep 2025 08:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: HA annex + order form language we need for procurement

Quick update — we can commit to providing the requested one-time telemetry package during the pilot (baseline month + 30 days) that includes per-route latency histograms, token-level cost breakouts, and aggregated regional availability tables. A few notes for drafting:

- For the order form, we should avoid absolute language that suggests an SLA-backed credit outside of the Order Form’s scope unless the customer purchases a Dedicated capacity add-on. For hosted accounts, credits will be as per the order form availability exhibit.
- We can offer a managed warm-standby profile (eu-west-1 / us-east-1) as an upsell with a documented failover playbook; if EdgeBank wants guaranteed cold-to-warm time below X minutes we should treat that as a Dedicated feature
- On latency measurement: specify the measurement window (monthly), percentile (p95), and exclusion windows for scheduled maintenance and customer-generated traffic spikes (we need precise definitions)

I’ll prep the telemetry list as an appendix to Marcus’ draft.

—Aditya
Aditya Rao
Principal Account Exec | Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.ai

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Gonzalez <anna.gonzalez@edgebank.com>, EdgeBank Procurement <procurement@edgebank.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@reditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 10 Sep 2025 17:24:00 -0700
Subject: Draft: HA Annex + order form snippets for EdgeBank (attached)

Anna / procurement team —

Attached is a first-pass HA Annex and suggested order form language. Highlights / deviations called out up-front so you and legal can triage: 

1) Availability and credits: We’ve mapped three availability tiers to a credit schedule in the order form (table on pg.2). For hosted customers we offer the order-form exhibit; Dedicated/reserved capacity customers can negotiate tighter credits and regional SLAs.

2) Latency commitments: Draft sets p95 targets at 250ms for <512 tokens and 450ms for >=512 tokens (measured at the API edge before any client-side batching). Measurement method and exclusion windows are in Section 3.

3) Failover behavior: Redwood will route to a warm standby region when regional capacity falls below the operational threshold. Warm standby is defined as a provisioned pool with KV-cache synchronization; failover time is expected to be within 5–15 minutes depending on model size and cache state. If EdgeBank requires deterministic <5 minute recovery, we recommend Dedicated warm-standby licensing.

4) Evidence and telemetry: As requested, we included an onboarding evidence checklist (per-route latency histograms, token cost by route, audit log export) and a one-time telemetry export window (baseline month + 30 days).

5) Exceptions: Scheduled maintenance windows and customer-driven traffic surges are excluded; we included language clarifying monitoring thresholds and notification cadence.

Next steps:
- Kimberly to review annex exceptions language and legal carve-outs
- Anna / procurement to provide EdgeBank’s order form template (if different from the attached) and any redlines
- I’ll prepare a DocuSign packet once legal alignment is done

Thanks — 
Marcus
[Attachment: HA_Annex_Draft_v1.docx, EdgeBank_OrderForm_v3.pdf]

From: Anna Gonzalez <anna.gonzalez@edgebank.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: EdgeBank Procurement <procurement@edgebank.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Sep 2025 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft: HA Annex + order form snippets for EdgeBank (attached)

Marcus — thanks for the draft. Procurement and infra ran this past our legal and ops — high-level feedback and requested redlines below: 

- Latency: strong preference to cap p95 for <512 tokens at 200ms in us-east-1 during baseline throughput; can tolerate 350ms for long sequences. If Redwood can meet 200ms p95 we’re willing to accept the credit schedule as written.
- Failover: please tighten the failover window language. We need a documented RTO objective for automated failover to warm-standby and a runbook entry that describes the rollback path. If automatic routing exceeds 10 minutes we need a defined manual mitigation process.
- Evidence: procurement requests that audit logs be retained for 13 months (internal policy). Also ask that telemetry exports be delivered as signed CSVs with a checksum and a point of contact for validation.
- Data residency: EdgeBank requires a written affirmation that customer production state and logs for EdgeBank accounts in this deal will remain in us-east-1 and not be processed in other regions except for the warm-standby failover path.

We’ll attach a redlined order form next. Can you provide an updated annex and order-form snippet addressing the four points above by Tue 9/16? We’re trying to close the procurement queue before the end of the month.

Anna Gonzalez
Director, Cloud Procurement | EdgeBank
[Attachment: EdgeBank_OrderForm_v3_Redline.pdf (pdf)]
